mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A double-digit year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by RSAFS) combined with a simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals a significant weakening in aggregate demand, which depresses earnings expectations and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY < -10% AND HOUST monthly < previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue and profit growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in CPIAUCSL above 6% combined with a federal funds rate below 1% signals an unexpected inflation shock with accommodative policy, which erodes real corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 6% AND FEDFUNDS < 1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent quarterly decline in real GDP (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals a macroeconomic downturn, which reduces earnings and increases risk aversion, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals an acceleration in labor market tightness, which boosts wage growth and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) below their respective 12-month moving averages signals a broad-based collapse in residential and consumer demand, which depresses corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-mo MA AND HOUST < 12-mo MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
